neighbours.label: inconceivability of removal: imagining or conceiving of something without a part of it ('hard to imagine X without Y', 'can't conceive of', 'X without Y seems incomplete', 'what if you took Y out of X'); the plain, possible sense of imagine/conceive stays quiet
fire: It is impossible to picture Naples without the roar of its scooters and the smell of frying dough.
Try to imagine the Beatles without Ringo; the songs would still exist, but the swing would be gone.
A Sunday roast without the crackling seems somehow unfinished to my grandmother.
Nobody at the firm can conceive of the newsroom without Helen barking from the corner desk.
What if you removed the monsoon from the story of Kerala? The whole calendar of festivals would collapse.
It is hard to imagine a Russian novel without a long scene at a railway station.
I cannot imagine our village without the Tuesday market; it is the only reason anyone meets.
The old editor said she could not conceive of a newspaper without a crossword.
quiet: It is easy to picture Naples in summer: the roar of scooters and the smell of frying dough everywhere.
Imagine the Beatles in 1963, playing three shows a night in a sweaty club in Hamburg.
A Sunday roast with crackling is my grandmother's idea of a perfect afternoon.
Everyone at the firm can picture the newsroom at six, with Helen barking from the corner desk.
The monsoon arrives in Kerala in early June and fills the whole calendar with festivals.
I can imagine several ways to open a Russian novel, but a railway station is the classic one.
I remember our village on Tuesdays, when the market is the only reason anyone meets.
The old editor said she could easily picture a newspaper run entirely by students.
